toc.title: The governance tools at a glance

html:
1The governance tools at a glance

Tool Purpose in one line Answers the question
Microsoft Purview Govern, protect and manage your data across the organization and find compliance risks "Where is our data, how sensitive is it, and are we compliant?"
Azure Policy Enforce rules on resources so they stay compliant "Are our resources configured the way we require?"
Resource locks Prevent accidental deletion or change of a resource "How do we stop someone deleting this by mistake?"

Exam tip

. Policy = what is allowed in the configuration. RBAC (Module 9) = who is allowed to act. Locks = protect from delete or change, even for an Owner.

2Microsoft Purview

Microsoft Purview is a family of data governance, risk and compliance solutions. It gives one view of data across on-premises, multicloud and software-as-a-service sources.

Capability What it does
Data discovery and catalog Scans and maps data sources, builds an inventory (data map) and a searchable catalog with classifications
Data classification and labeling Finds sensitive data (for example credit card numbers) and applies sensitivity labels
Data protection Helps prevent data loss and control sharing
Compliance management Helps measure and manage compliance against regulations and standards (for example with a compliance score)
Data lineage Shows where data comes from and how it moves

Use Purview when a question is about knowing, classifying and governing data and compliance risk, not about configuring Azure resources.

Exam tip

. "Discover and classify sensitive data across the whole organization" → Purview. "Enforce that VMs can only be created in approved regions" → Azure Policy.

3Azure Policy

Azure Policy helps you enforce organizational standards and assess compliance at scale. It evaluates your resources against rules and shows which ones are compliant or non-compliant.

Examples of policy rules:

  • Only allow resources in approved regions.
  • Only allow certain VM sizes.
  • Require a tag (such as CostCenter) on every resource.
  • Require encryption or specific settings.
Concept Meaning
Policy definition The rule and the effect (what happens when the rule is not met)
Initiative A group of policy definitions managed together toward one goal (for example a compliance standard)
Assignment Applying a definition or initiative to a scope (management group, subscription, resource group)
Effects Deny (block the action), Audit (flag it), Modify/Append (change or add a property such as a tag), DeployIfNotExists (create a missing resource)
Remediation Fix existing non-compliant resources
  • Assignments are inherited down the hierarchy (Module 5).
  • Policy evaluates resource properties. It does not give or remove user permissions; that is RBAC.
  • A policy can block a non-compliant request even from an Owner.
Exam tip

. Deny blocks creation; audit only reports. Initiative = bundle of policies. A policy assigned at a management group applies to all subscriptions below.

4Resource locks

A resource lock prevents accidental deletion or modification of an Azure resource, resource group or subscription.

Lock type What it blocks Allowed
Delete (CanNotDelete) Deleting Reading and modifying
Read-only Deleting and modifying Reading only

Key facts:

  • Locks apply to all users and roles, even Owners. To change or delete a locked resource you must remove the lock first (which needs permission to manage locks).
  • Locks are inherited: a lock on a resource group applies to every resource in it, including ones added later.
  • A read-only lock can cause surprising effects (for example you may be unable to start a stopped VM or list keys). Beyond the study guide
  • Locks protect against management-plane actions, not data changes inside a service (for example writing a blob).
Exam tip

. "Protect a production resource group from being deleted by mistake" → delete lock on the resource group. "Even the subscription Owner cannot delete it" → lock.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors must ensure that every resource is created only in the East US and West Europe regions. Which service enforces this?

  • AMicrosoft Purview
  • BAzure Monitor
  • CAzure Policy
  • DAzure Advisor
Show the answer

Answer: C. Azure Policy evaluates and can deny resources that break a rule such as allowed locations.

S2A production resource group must be protected from accidental deletion, even by an Owner. What should be applied?

  • AA tag called Protected
  • BA delete lock on the resource group
  • CA budget alert
  • DA Reader role assignment
Show the answer

Answer: B. A delete lock blocks deletion for all users until the lock is removed. Tags have no protective effect.

S3A company wants to find and classify sensitive data such as card numbers across on-premises and cloud sources. Which service fits?

  • AMicrosoft Purview
  • BAzure Policy
  • CAzure DNS
  • DResource locks
Show the answer

Answer: A. Purview discovers, classifies and governs data and helps manage compliance risk.

S4What is an initiative in Azure Policy?

  • AA single permission given to one user
  • BA group of policy definitions managed together
  • CA type of lock on a resource group
  • DA cost report for each subscription
Show the answer

Answer: B. An initiative bundles related policy definitions toward one goal.

S5A policy has the Audit effect and a VM is created that breaks the rule. What happens?

  • AThe creation is blocked and an error is shown
  • BThe VM is deleted automatically after one hour
  • CThe subscription is disabled until the VM is fixed
  • DThe VM is created and flagged as non-compliant
Show the answer

Answer: D. Audit reports non-compliance without blocking. Deny would block.

S6Which lock type allows a resource to be changed but not deleted?

  • ARead-only
  • BDelete (CanNotDelete)
  • CTag lock
  • DPolicy lock
Show the answer

Answer: B. A delete lock prevents deletion; modification is still allowed. A read-only lock blocks both.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of Azure Policy?

Show the answer

Enforce organizational standards and assess resource compliance.

R2What does Microsoft Purview do?

Show the answer

Governs and protects data across the organization and helps manage compliance.

R3Name the two lock types.

Show the answer

Delete (CanNotDelete) and Read-only.

R4Do locks apply to Owners?

Show the answer

Yes. The lock must be removed first.

R5What is a policy initiative?

Show the answer

A group of policy definitions assigned together.

R6Policy or RBAC: which controls who may act?

Show the answer

RBAC. Policy controls what resource configurations are allowed.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purview data governance and compliance: discover, classify, label, lineage, across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS
Azure Policy rules for resources: deny, audit, modify, deployIfNotExists; initiatives bundle policies; inherited
Locks delete lock or read-only lock; even Owners blocked; inherited; remove the lock first
Policy vs RBAC policy = allowed configuration; RBAC = allowed people and actions
